capabilities.target: Engineering design docs (confidential, write-restricted to engineers)
Chat reply to the SSO-authenticated requester

inputs.source: Employee question submitted via SSO-authenticated chat client
Engineering design docs indexed for docs.search; write access restricted to engineers

instructions.note: The instruction 'Answer engineering questions using docs.search' does not restrict responses to requesters authorized to view confidential design docs. Any SSO-authenticated employee, not only engineers, can receive confidential content through the agent.

The only control against leaking secrets/credentials is a behavioral prompt instruction ('Never paste secrets or credentials into answers'). There is no structural redaction or output filter, and the instruction's wording covers literal secrets/credentials only, not confidential content in general.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials
controls.decay_rationale: Behavioral instruction; a more capable model can rationalize exceptions. Its scope is also limited to literal secrets/credentials, not general confidential design-doc content, so it provides no coverage against exfiltration of non-credential confidential text.

controls.name: Reply destination bound to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: Destination comes from the authenticated session record, not from model output, so it cannot be redirected to a third party by prompt content. Does not decay with model capability. Only covers the chat_reply channel, not any future egress-capable tool.

controls.name: No network egress capability exists today
controls.decay_rationale: Currently independent because no tool exists that can reach an attacker-controlled destination. This is an absence-of-capability state rather than a robust allowlist, so per control_decay.md (network egress allowlist row) it fails outright, not just weakens, the moment any new egress-capable tool such as web.fetch is added (trigger: new_tool).

controls.name: Read-only credential for docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: Scoped credential; does not decay with model capability. Prevents write/delete on design docs but does not prevent a read-then-exfiltrate pattern if an egress channel exists.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Client-side rendering restriction blocks automatic fetch-on-render exfiltration (e.g., markdown image tags) independent of model capability. Does not cover a dedicated fetch tool such as the planned web.fetch, which is a server-side capability, not a client rendering behavior.

controls.name: Destination allowlist for the planned web.fetch tool
controls.decay_rationale: If implemented as a vetted, non-model-writable allowlist of destinations, this would remain independent of model capability and would sever the exfiltration channel that web.fetch would otherwise open.

controls.name: Provenance tagging for Jira-sourced content
controls.decay_rationale: If provenance is enforced at the retrieval/store layer (not written by the model), tagging customer-authored ticket content as untrusted (U) and blocking its treatment as instructions stays independent of model capability.

controls.name: Authentication and definition pinning for the planned Jira MCP server
controls.decay_rationale: Peer identity verification and pinned/hashed tool definitions for the new MCP server prevent spoofing and rug-pull tampering independent of model capability, though they do not by themselves neutralize injected instructions inside legitimate customer ticket text.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) on web.fetch calls derived from confidential content
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action review gate showing the full destination URL and payload, bound to review before the call executes, does not decay with model capability, unlike a gate that shows only a model-written summary.

findings.title: Present state: docs-qa reply path is low risk because no egress channel exists today

evidence.observation: 'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.' No current capability can move data to an attacker-reachable destination.

'Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links.' Reply destination is bound to the authenticated session and there is no passive rendering-based exfiltration channel.

recommendations.action: Before shipping any tool with network reach (e.g., web.fetch) or any new data source (e.g., a Jira MCP server), re-run this assessment and add a destination allowlist plus provenance tagging for newly ingested untrusted content.

findings.title: Forecast lethal trifecta (TC1): customer-authored Jira tickets + confidential design docs + planned web.fetch egress

attack_path.note: Confidential engineering design docs, currently read only via cap.docs_search.
Existing least-privilege read capability; unchanged in scope by the roadmap.

Roadmap: a Jira MCP server including tickets filed by customers becomes a new untrusted (U) input read into agent context; a customer can embed injected instructions in a ticket body (indirect prompt injection).

Roadmap: web.fetch creates a new egress channel; a hijacked agent can construct a URL whose query string encodes confidential design-doc content and fetch it, sending the data to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

evidence.observation: 'Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.' Neither the new egress tool nor the new untrusted input source exists yet, so today's path is not complete; the finding models the risk that opens once both ship.
'There is no network egress today.' This absence-of-capability control is exactly what the new_tool trigger defeats, per control_decay.md's network egress allowlist row.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, add a destination allowlist that excludes attacker-writable or arbitrary destinations; do not allow the model to choose an unconstrained URL.

Tag all content ingested from the Jira MCP server, especially customer-authored ticket text, as untrusted (U) with enforced provenance, and ensure instruction-like directives found in ticket bodies are never executed.
Require authenticated, peer-identity-verified, and definition-pinned connection for the new Jira MCP server before connecting it.
Add a human approval gate with raw-action review (full URL and payload visible, not a collapsed model summary) before any web.fetch call whose arguments were derived from confidential-tagged content.
Log and alert on web.fetch calls whose URL or query string contains high-entropy strings or content flagged as derived from confidential design docs.

governance_refs.note: Adding a new tool (web.fetch) and a new MCP server (Jira) are significant changes requiring reassessment before deployment.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff adding an outbound network tool (e.g., 'web.fetch', 'http.get'), or MCP client config diff adding a Jira server entry. Per control_decay.md, either change should trigger reassessment before release.

rating.rationale: Today docs-qa is low risk on both inherent and residual bases: the only source with elevated trust concern is internal (confidential design docs), the reply path is bound to the authenticated requester, and no capability today can move data to an attacker-reachable destination (runtime notes: 'no network egress today'). That single absence-of-egress condition is a structural, independent control that currently severs any exfiltration path (ctl.no_network_egress, ctl.reply_recipient_binding). The roadmap explicitly plans to add web.fetch (a new egress-capable tool) and a Jira MCP server that ingests customer-authored (untrusted) ticket content in the same sprint. Per control_decay.md, an empty egress surface is defeated outright, not merely weakened, by the new_tool trigger, and none of the other current controls (read-only credential, no-markdown-rendering, the secrets-only prompt instruction) cover the new web.fetch channel or validate Jira-sourced content as untrusted. Once both roadmap items ship, an untrusted source (customer ticket) reaching an S3 sink (irreversible egress of confidential data) with no effective preventive control yields critical projected risk. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.no_network_egress.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.
No formal tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability and control details are inferred from prose runtime notes, so confidence on several fields is medium rather than high.

The web.fetch tool and the Jira MCP server are roadmap items not yet implemented; their exact design (authentication, argument schema, egress scoping) is unknown, so the forecast assumes a typical, currently-unscoped implementation of each per the toxic_combinations.md guidance for additive triggers.
Whether Jira ticket text would automatically enter the agent's context on every query, or only on explicit retrieval, is assumed based on typical MCP tool behavior and is not confirmed by a manifest.
